getStateDotColor is a faithful native slice of @/types/fsm getStateColor: VARIANT_DOT maps the 5 BadgeVariants to their Tailwind v3 dot hex (success #4ade80, warning #fbbf24, danger #f87171, info #60a5fa, neutral #9ca3af); FSM_STATE_DOTS ports the {variant, dot-override?} for ALL 8 FSMs (vehicle, drive_session, charge_session, command, notification, alert_cooldown, automation, telemetry_connection) exactly as web/src/types/fsm/*.ts defines them (e.g. vehicle.charging->cyan-400, vehicle.parked->purple-400, automation.retrying keeps the warning default amber while command/notification.retrying override to purple-400, automation.disabled->red-400/50 rgba). Resolution mirrors the source: unknown fsmType falls back to the vehicle FSM, state is looked up via state.toLowerCase(), unknown states return the neutral default — and only the .dot channel is materialized because that is the only field this component consumes. badgeDot/bg/text overrides are intentionally not ported (unused here).

No DOM-only modules, browser HTML elements, Recharts, Leaflet, framer-motion, lucide-react, or old web UI components are imported — only React (useMemo/useRef), react-native primitives (Pressable, StyleSheet, View, type DimensionValue), the existing native AppText, theme tokens (colors/spacing/typography), and the type-only FSMTransition from the ported native useFSM hook. State names (ticks/end/start/hasHint/showWiden/showJump/isSelected/leftPct), the i18n keys + fallbacks + interpolation args, the window/unit math (minutes, 60_000 ms, leftPct %), and the visual intent (axis + colored dots, selected ring, empty-state hint + widen/jump actions) are all preserved. No API paths exist in this presentational component. Gates run from apps/native: npm run typecheck PASS; npm run lint -- --quiet PASS; npm test -- --runInBand --detectOpenHandles PASS (StateTimeline.test.tsx, 9 tests).
